lines.cap: He did it all. Bootleg booze, bribes, and bodies. But in the end, they nailed him on his books.
lines.say: He did it all. Bootleg booze, bribes, and bodies. But in the end, they nailed him on his books.

lines.cap: Al Capone. Chicago, the 1920s. Selling illegal alcohol made his gang an estimated hundred million dollars a year.
lines.say: Al Capone. Chicago, the 1920s. Selling illegal alcohol made his gang an estimated hundred million dollars a year.

lines.cap: Police couldn't touch him. Witnesses kept forgetting things. Or disappearing.
lines.say: Police couldn't touch him. Witnesses kept forgetting things. Or disappearing.

lines.cap: In 1929, seven men from a rival gang were lined up against a garage wall and shot. The Saint Valentine's Day Massacre. Capone? In Florida, working on his tan.
lines.say: In 1929, seven men from a rival gang were lined up against a garage wall and shot. The Saint Valentine's Day Massacre. Capone? In Florida, working on his tan.

lines.cap: He even ran a free soup kitchen during the Great Depression. Feeding thousands. Great PR.
lines.say: He even ran a free soup kitchen during the Great Depression. Feeding thousands. Great PR.

lines.cap: So the government tried the most boring weapon there is. Taxes. Capone had never filed a return.
lines.say: So the government tried the most boring weapon there is. Taxes. Capone had never filed a return.

lines.cap: A small team of accountants followed his money for two years. In 1931, the most feared man in America got eleven years, for tax evasion.
lines.say: A small team of accountants followed his money for two years. In 1931, the most feared man in America got eleven years, for tax evasion.
